fields.v: Wang, S. (2026). Agent Team Work Zone: An Automated, Persistent Workspace for Long-Lived Claude Code Agent Teams. arXiv:2607.22917v2 [cs.AI], 30 Jul 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2607.22917v2 [cs.AI], 30 Jul 2026; no published venue stated
Case Western Reserve University (single author)

Proposes an approach; secondary: Conceptual — ATWZ, a file-based persistence and management layer over Claude Code Agent Teams, presented as a developer-oriented design manual (no benchmarks or user studies; illustrated by scenarios and dogfooding)

Agent Team Work Zone (ATWZ), open source; releases v0.1.0 (frozen, Claude Code <= 2.1.177) and v0.2.0+ for Claude Code >= 2.1.178; v0.3.2 current as of July 2026. Built on Claude Code Agent Teams (experimental feature)

Per-agent 'workstation' directories under _agent_team_work_zone/: README.md (role + work rules), notes.md, TODO.md, ACTIVE_JOBS.md, COMPLETED_JOBS.md; team workstations add TEAMMATE_INFO.json (registry), roundtable/ (team messages), team_recipes/, teammates/<name>/ (README, working-context.md, completed.md, TODO.md, commitments.md); checkpoint file (current-state snapshot + append-only journal); meeting_room/ markdown messages with frontmatter status OPEN -> IN_PROGRESS -> RESOLVED; handoff packages; skills, hooks and scripts

Team lifecycle rather than a development flow: /onboard -> (/promote-to-team) -> /spawn-team (collect task, decompose, propose lineup, user confirms, spawn) -> active loop with automatic checkpoints (TeammateIdle hook, 15-minute threshold) -> bench/offboard -> /reactivate-team after session end; messaging via /check-inbox and /handoff; read-only plan gate before larger teammate changes
User confirms the proposed team lineup; user confirms inbox items before they run; lead approves teammates' read-only plans before larger changes; 'human in the loop throughout'

Design, not an evaluation: no measurement of benefit, no comparison with alternatives, no user study. Known gaps: checkpoint gate fails open for brand-new teammates; checkpoint writer/reader contract is a documentation convention, not checked; some detections rely on text patterns. Future: empirical evaluation of recovery reliability under real interruptions, overhead and usability; tighter lead/teammate protocol; less prompt-writing; more autonomous mode
